reason: Both conversations reached the correct, appropriately hedged diagnosis (iced evaporator from a defrost-system fault), prescribed a full 24-48h manual defrost with no ice-chipping, and escalated to an engineer if it recurs, and neither named a part number or asked for the full model. Conversation 2 was more disciplined: it asked one targeted question at a time, confirmed the key evidence (thick frost on the freezer back wall, weak vent airflow) before committing, and explicitly told the owner an engineer must test the heater/sensor/control rather than replace parts by guesswork. Conversation 1 opened with a long generic checklist partly in US units and never asked about frost on the panel, though it added genuinely useful extras (food-safety advice at 12C, warranty check, fan listen test, drain flush) that narrow the gap.
